layout.unified_cross_account_description: Combine every signed-in account in "All inboxes". Off keeps the unified views inside the active account and its shared folders.

licences.app_desc: The app is free software under the {licence}. You can use, study, share and change it.

email.app_icon_badge_desc: Show the inbox unread count as a badge on the app icon.
email.mute_account_desc: No alerts for new mail in this account. Long-press a folder in the sidebar to mute or unmute it on its own.
email.sound_channel_hint: Sound and vibration for mail alerts are controlled by the Android notification channel: long-press a notification or open the system app settings.

push.accounts_desc_mobile: Background notifications of each signed-in account on this device. Switch to an account to turn them on or off for it.
push.confirm_disable_message_mobile: This device will stop receiving new-mail alerts for this account.
push.description_mobile: Receive system notifications for new mail when the app is closed. Delivered via the Bulwark push relay; the relay never sees mail content.
push.err_android_only: Push notifications are only available on Android.
push.err_apns_empty: iOS returned an empty push token.
push.err_apns_token: iOS could not issue a push token ({detail}).
push.err_fcm_empty: Firebase returned an empty device token.
push.err_fcm_token: Firebase could not issue a device token ({detail}). Push over FCM needs Google Play services on this device.
push.err_fcm_token_up: Firebase could not issue a device token ({detail}). Push over FCM needs Google Play services on this device. This device has a UnifiedPush distributor installed - switch the delivery method to UnifiedPush instead.
push.err_forbidden: The mail server doesn't allow background notifications for this account.
push.err_jmap_list: Could not read the push registrations from the mail server: {detail}
push.err_jmap_refused: The mail server refused the push subscription: {detail}
push.err_no_account: No account loaded - cannot set up push.
push.err_over_quota: This account has too many push registrations on the mail server (the limit is usually 15). Revoke devices you no longer use in the notification settings, then try again.
push.err_relay_https: The relay URL must use https://.
push.err_relay_no_apns: The push relay at {url} does not deliver to iPhones and iPads yet.
push.err_relay_rejected: The push relay rejected the registration: {detail}
push.err_relay_unreachable: Could not reach the push relay at {url} ({detail}).
push.err_up_android_only: UnifiedPush is only available on Android.
push.err_url_refused: The mail server refuses to send notifications to the relay at {url}. It only accepts https addresses on a public domain name, not a private IP address or a local name such as localhost, .local or .lan. Use the hosted relay, or give your relay a public domain name.
push.err_verify_rejected: The mail server rejected the verification code: {detail}
push.err_verify_relay: The relay never received the verification code from the mail server (last relay response: {detail}).
push.err_verify_timeout: The mail server did not send a verification code to the relay within 75 s. Check that the server can reach the relay URL.
push.relay_desc_mobile: The server that delivers your notifications. Defaults to the hosted Bulwark relay; change only if you self-host. Must use https.
push.shared_mailboxes_no_push: Mailboxes others share with you don't send background notifications.
push.status_android_only: Background notifications are available on Android only.
push.transport_desc: How notifications reach this device: Google’s Firebase Cloud Messaging, or a UnifiedPush distributor app (such as ntfy) for Google-free delivery.
push.up_distributor_desc: Several UnifiedPush distributor apps are installed - pick the one that should deliver notifications.
push.up_no_distributor: No UnifiedPush distributor app is installed on this device. Install one (for example ntfy) and try again.

offline.description: Download recent messages so they open instantly and remain readable without a connection. Bodies only — attachments are still fetched on demand.
offline.description_short: Keep recent messages on this phone so they open without a connection.
offline.enabled_desc: When on, the app keeps message bodies for the selected window on this device.
offline.max_size_desc: Oldest messages are removed when the cache grows past this.

offline.window_desc: How far back to cache, measured by message receipt date.

plugins.mobile_description: Plugins run inside the webmail and extend it in the browser.
plugins.mobile_explainer: The mobile app has no plugin runtime. Install and manage plugins from the webmail under Settings → Plugins; themes and filters they provide are not applied here.

privacy.favicons: Sender icons for business mail come from DuckDuckGo's icon service, which sees the sender's domain. Turn them off under Appearance → Sender favicons.
privacy.no_tracking: The app has no analytics and no ads.
privacy.phone_backup: None of it goes into Android's cloud backup.
privacy.phone_secure: Your sign-in details are kept in the system's secure storage. Settings, the offline mail cache and changes waiting to sync are kept in the app's own storage.
privacy.push: When notifications are on, your server tells the push relay ({relay}) that something changed, and the relay wakes the app through {service}. The relay sees a device token and a change marker, never your mail. You can use your own relay under Notifications.
privacy.server: Mail, calendars, contacts and files are loaded from your server and saved back to it. Apart from the connections below, the app talks only to your server.
privacy.updates: The app asks GitHub for the latest release to tell you about updates.
privacy.updates_android: The app asks GitHub for the latest release to tell you about updates. Turn that off under Updates.

client_cert.clear_message: New requests will no longer present a certificate. The certificate stays installed in Android.
client_cert.description: Picks an installed Android certificate to authenticate to the server during the TLS handshake. Useful when the reverse proxy enforces mTLS.
client_cert.hint: Install the certificate via Android Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials, then pick it here.

credentials.allowed_ips_hint: Comma or space separated. Leave empty to allow any IP.

security.restricted: Your server lets only apps its administrator approved change the password, two-factor sign-in, app passwords and API keys. Bulwark signed in without that approval, so mail, contacts, calendars and files work, but these settings don't. Change them in your server's web interface or the Bulwark webmail.
